The one-port waveguide method measures complex permittivity and permeability of RAMs over broad frequency bands.
The method is suitable for magnetic and medium- to high-loss materials.
The measurement setup operates at 5.8 to 8.2 GHz (J-band).
The system uses a network analyzer (Agilent 8363e VNA) and a waveguide with a sliding short.
Reflection coefficients are measured at multiple positions of the sliding short.
The method is based on transmission line theory, rectangular waveguide theory, two-port network fraction linear transformation, and the odd-even mode method.
Calibration involves the S-O-L-T error correction procedure.
The error analysis uses an adaptive differential evolution (DE) algorithm to estimate the upper limit error.
The method is nondestructive and does not alter the material being tested.
Three samples were measured: air, P VP-Fe3+, and nano-FeNiO.
Each sample has a thickness greater than 2 mm.
The method is validated with measurements of air and typical RAM samples.
The method is competitive for RAM characterization due to its accuracy and nondestructive nature.
The measurement procedure includes calibration, loading the material, and measuring reflection coefficients at multiple positions.
The error analysis considers random reading errors, displacement errors, and dimensional errors.
The DE algorithm provides a global search capability and robust error estimation.
The method is applicable to a wide range of RAMs and can be used in various applications such as compact test ranges and RCS minimization.
The paper references several other methods for determining permittivity and permeability, including split-cylinder resonators, cavity resonators, and transmission-line techniques.
The method is described in detail with a derivation flow chart and measurement model.
The software for data acquisition and computation is specifically programmed for this method.
The method is suitable for both homogeneous and layered materials.
The results show that the method is effective for characterizing the properties of RAMs.
